What each source code means in each dataset

Source: R/variables.R
soil_variable_mappings.Rd

One row per mapping of a source code to a variable: the original code and label of the provider, its unit and procedure as the source gives them, and how the hub judged the mapping (semantic_status, unit_status, unit_evidence). Original terms are kept: no unit is converted, no label rewritten.

Usage

soil_variable_mappings(soil = soil_session(), ...)

Arguments

soil

A session (the default session when omitted), or the result of soil_variables(), whose mappings are then listed without a request. Client-side: not sent to the API.

...

The filters of soil_variables() (code, domain, measurement_kind, target_level, dataset, provider, available_only) when soil is a session. API query parameters of GET /variables, as for soil_variables().

Value

A data frame, one row per (variable, dataset, mapping): variable_code, provider_code, dataset_code, source_code, source_official_code, source_label, source_unit, procedure_code, procedure_description, source_value_kind, mapping_status, semantic_status, unit_status, unit_evidence (list), source_scope, source_notes, documentation_url, method_facets (list of data frames facet_key, facet_value, element_count, source_dataset_counts).

Details

Terms: source_code is the code of the source as stored, source_official_code the provider's official spelling; source_scope limits a mapping to one source dataset (e.g. "<SOTWIS package>/") when the same code means something different there; method_facets are the facets of the WoSIS methods that change the meaning of a value.

Rights: soil:summary.

See also

Other discovery: soil_api_info(), soil_capabilities(), soil_citations(), soil_code_list(), soil_code_lists(), soil_countries(), soil_country(), soil_dataset(), soil_datasets(), soil_formats(), soil_ttr_flag_legend(), soil_variables()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
m <- soil_variable_mappings(soil, dataset = "sotwis_polygons")
m[m$unit_status != "documented", c("variable_code", "source_code", "source_unit", "source_notes")]
} # }
